en: The Ritual Manual for the Secret Accomplishment of Śakrasyaśaila,
Spoken by the Buddha. Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of Reception,
and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, Subject Shi Hu, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
At that time, Śākyamuni Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets, saying:
"You should now know that to the north of the village of Āmra in the kingdom of Magadha, there is Mount Vaidehī."
There is the Śakrakaṇṭha Rock;
within that rock are ninety-nine palaces,
where a multitude of one koṭi great bodhisattvas resides.
The eight classes of devas and nāgas, as well as various ṛṣis and celestial beings,
dwell therein. The Bodhisattva Maitreya currently resides there,
having entered the samādhi named "Supreme Adornment."
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he taught the Dharma to instruct the assembly of bodhisattvas.
Vajrapāṇi, this Śakrāśmaka Rock is most supreme and excellent;
it is a miraculous transformation of the supernatural powers of all Buddhas.
This cannot be fathomed by those of limited intelligence;
it is a dharma-gate associated with the inconceivable,
wherein the great bodhisattvas dwell.
Therein exist various mundane noble dharmas associated with accomplishment.
If there is one who gives rise to a resolute mind seeking to proceed toward enlightenment,
diligently practicing all manner of deeds for incalculable eons without fearing the long duration of time—
I shall now proclaim these various methods of accomplishment for this Śakra Cave.
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who is free from greed, hatred, delusion, and the notion of a self,
who has subdued their sense faculties, and who gives rise to pure faith by relying upon the Buddha’s true teaching;
He then proclaimed for them:
"If there are those who commit various evil deeds,
fail to produce the seed of bodhi, and remain far removed from the True Dharma..."
"Do not speak this to those who do not believe in cause and effect, who slander their ācāryas, or who are unfilial toward their parents.
At that time, the Great Lord of Secrets, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, [spoke thus].
He addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, as the Buddha has taught, there is great merit;
this is a great skillful means that does not require deliberate effort."
"In this present life, one shall behold the Bodhisattva Maitreya.
I now desire to hear this; I pray that the Buddha will explain it for me.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the Great Lord of Secrets, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, saying:
I shall now explain this to you as it truly is.
Vajrapāṇi, if there are practitioners of the yoga who desire to enter that Śakrakaṇḍa cave, [they should proceed as follows].
Without relying on preparatory practices, one does not seek to behold the Bodhisattva Maitreya in this present life;
nor does one delight in seeking the teachings on the sacred sword, the sacred wheel, the wish-fulfilling gem,
the sacred medicine *añjana*, the *pānauka* elixir, or the sacred ornaments.
One who possesses such methods of accomplishment must first develop a mind of faith and reverence toward the ācārya and receive the transmission according to the dharma.
Thereafter, one should seek the majestic protection of one's own tutelary deity,
perform vast offerings to all the Tathāgatas,
and universally practice great generosity for the sake of all sentient beings.
The practitioner should first walk ten bow-lengths facing east;
then, turning westward, he should walk another thirty bow-lengths before entering a palace.
It was square in shape and provided with windows;
as soon as the traveler looked through the windows,
he beheld various kinds of trees.
The trees there are all sacred medicines.
Furthermore, one sees palaces belonging to the world-dwellers;
practitioners rest therein for a short while.
Not far from here, one sees a well;
it is as deep as half a person's height.
There is also an iron chain held by people, which serves as a ladder.
The practitioner should then firmly grasp this cord and descend two cubits (*hasta*) until reaching level ground.
The practitioner should then feel the ground with his hand.
Gradually, he saw a flight of stairs,
which the traveler descended;
next, he saw an *āmra* tree.
That tree bears fruit shaped like a conch shell.
A traveler should take one fruit, carry it outside, and eat it.
Having eaten it, he shall immediately attain an extension of life for one kalpa, equal to that of Nārāyaṇa.
Possessing the marks and signs of physical excellence, endowed with great power,
and having attained the dhāraṇīs that fully realize all Buddha-dharmas—
if the practitioner does not take up this fruit.
He then proceeded for a distance of one hundred bow-lengths and beheld the palace of Maheśvara.
Before that palace was a great pond filled with sacred medicinal herbs.
To the north of this pond there is a great tārā tree.
The traveler should then take a fruit from that tree, go outside, and eat it.
One will immediately attain an extension of life for one kalpa.
If the practitioner does not wish to take this fruit,
they may instead take a sacred medicine from within the pond.
Carrying it, one goes outside;
whatever objects one touches are all transformed into gold.
If the practitioner, however, does not wish to take this sacred elixir, [he may instead...]
Thereupon, taking one *harītakī* fruit from the four sides of that celestial palace and eating it outside,
he likewise attained an extension of his lifespan for one kalpa.
Thereafter, departing from that celestial palace,
he again saw two paths to the south and north; however,
he was unable to proceed along the southern path.
"You should travel toward the north.
Not far from here, you will see a copper city;
that city is both high and vast."
The practitioner should strike that city gate;
at that time, a Mātangī woman will open it for him.
Having entered, he will immediately see two paths.
On the path to his left was a great tree named Aśoka;
beneath that tree were many Mātangī women playing in the four directions.
Those many women then pointed out the path to the right for the practitioner.
The practitioner then proceeded toward the right side for one yojana.
Exhausting the range of his vision,
he saw from afar a silver city;
its walls were high and broad, and all its gates were secured with locks and keys.
There are door-hooks there shaped like snakes placed at the sides of the gates.
When a traveler sees them, he should not give rise to fear;
he should simply take one hook and open the gate himself.
Having entered, one first beholds the sacred sword.
If the practitioner wishes to take it, they should immediately seize that sword;
having grasped it, they immediately attain the status of a Great Vidyārāja.
After his life has ended, he will be reborn in Tuṣita Heaven.
If he does not wish to take this sword,
he shall instead take the noble wheel.
Having received it, one immediately attains the rank of a Cakravartin king;
after the end of life, one is reborn in the Heaven of the Four Great Kings.
If one does not wish to take up this wheel, [one may instead seek other fruits].
One should then take the wish-fulfilling jewel.
Having received it, one immediately attains the five supernatural powers and performs the eighteen transformations.
Spontaneously, a voice proclaims throughout the great earth to all sentient beings.
He spoke these words: "If there are sentient beings who have any need or request, I shall bestow it upon them so that all may have their wishes fulfilled.
He then established a wish-fulfilling jewel banner (*cintāmaṇi-dhvaja*). Upon seeing the Buddha's teachings, he [acted accordingly].
The practitioner should then open and look upon it;
they will thereby attain the dhāraṇī of all Buddha-dharmas without loss and thoroughly comprehend the dharma of the supreme ultimate truth.
If one sees the sacred medicine,
the practitioner should take one *liang* of it,
which can produce one *koṭi* of gold.
If one takes this medicine, one's lifespan will equal that of the Brahmā heavens.
If one sees a *pānuka* [plant],
the practitioner should take it.
Having put it on, he was able to travel throughout the four great continents at the time of sunrise and return to his original location within a short period of time.
If one sees añjana ointment,
the practitioner should take a small amount and apply it to his own eyes;
he will then be able to see all things within the three realms.
If one sees the ornaments of the noble ones,
the practitioner should take them and don them;
immediately, one will attain the majesty of the primary and secondary marks, and the mastery of invisibility.
If the practitioner does not wish to seek such methods of noble accomplishment,
they should simply rest and stay overnight in that place;
they shall know it to be night when the lotuses within that rock cave close.
When those asura women emerge to gather flowers, one immediately knows it is day;
at that time, the practitioner should proceed further.
Not far from here, he will see another golden city.
When the practitioner enters that city,
they immediately see palaces composed of the seven precious gems,
adorned with pillars of maṇi-jewels, precious wheels, jeweled nets, and various exquisite flowers.
Furthermore, it was draped above with networks of pearls;
the ground was strewn with golden sand, pure and delightful.
Upon that palace stood a lion throne, lofty, vast, and magnificent.
The Bodhisattva Maitreya sat upon his seat,
surrounded with reverence by countless devas, nāgas, the eight classes of supernatural beings, and hosts of sages.
They listen to and receive the sublime Dharma proclaimed by the Bodhisattva.
At that time, once the practitioner has arrived there,
they immediately give rise to a most supreme and rarefied mind, approach the Bodhisattva, pay homage, and stand before them.
At that time, Maitreya Bodhisattva said to the practitioner,
"Welcome, son of good family.
The practitioner should then reply:
"Welcome to you now.
The Bodhisattva spoke again: "Excellent, excellent, son of good family!
You have been able to give rise to a courageous and firm resolve to come here."
Why is this? Because the sentient beings of Jambudvīpa possess firm and steadfast faith;
they are able to apply themselves with diligent vigor toward the Buddha-dharma, and they are able to give rise to a mind of reverence toward me.
"You should now know that if any sentient beings wish to behold my body in this present life or in a future birth,
they should generate a resolute mind and recite my root vidyā-mantra."
One will immediately attain peace and happiness, be free from all calamities, and behold my body.
The root mantra is as follows:
*Namaḥ ratnatrayāya* (Homage to the Triple Gem). *Namaḥ vairo*... [the rest of the mantra].
Tadyathā: Oṃ maitrī tathāgatāya arhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya tathāha | oṃ maitrī-tri maitrīvāsini maitre.
*Duḥ-dṛṣṭa-ghātaya samara samara svāka-pratijñāya sara sara visara visara mardaya mardaya mardanotu.*
GATE (14) MAHĀPRATIBHĀNATE MANASI SVAHĀ (15). The Bodhisattva said:
"Noble son, this great vidyā now possesses immense power.
If any practitioners of yoga can generate a resolute mind and recite this vidyā, [they shall attain success]."
"This person shall certainly and without doubt behold my body.
Furthermore, Maitreya Bodhisattva addressed the practitioner, saying:
"Why have you come here now? What do you seek?"
Do you seek to behold my person and hear the true Dharma?
Or do you seek various methods of spiritual accomplishment (*siddhi*)?
Or perhaps you seek great renown throughout Jambudvīpa?
"I shall grant the boon you seek. The practitioner replied, "O Bodhisattva,
from the time I first resolved upon the path until my entry into this palace, I have done so solely for the purpose of seeking an audience with you, the Bodhisattva."
I have now attained the vision of the mind and am fully satisfied; nothing else is sought by me.
As I dwell here until the Bodhisattva comes and attains perfect enlightenment, may I be present before that Bodhisattva.
They listened to and received the true Dharma.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi,
having heard Śākyamuni Buddha preach this Dharma, [acted accordingly].
Rejoicing, they received it with faith and practiced in accordance with the teachings.
The *Buddhabhāṣita-Śakrasya-guhya-siddhi-vidhi*.
